claim: Brazil's pavilion at Web Summit has its programme on three days, 10 to 12 November.
Diario de Pernambuco reported on 23 June 2026 that more than 45 Brazilian companies, most from Pernambuco, have used Cais do Porto since it started in 2024.
Cais do Porto, in Aveiro, is the international unit of Recife's technology park Porto Digital.
ApexBrasil and Sebrae run a startup incubator in Lisbon, which names its second class on 10 November.
Unicorn Factory Lisboa has signed partnerships with Instituto Caldeira, Cubo and Sai do Papel, as its head Gil Azevedo told ECO in April 2025.
On 13 November 2023, during Web Summit, Sebrae's president, Décio Lima, signed a memorandum of understanding with Startup Portugal.
DN Brasil reported on 22 June 2026 that a second group of ten Pernambuco companies arrived in June 2026 through Porto Digital's internationalisation programme.
On 30 June, Porto Digital, Cais do Porto and CONSECTI signed a cooperation agreement, as TI Inside reported.
In November 2024, Brazil's ambassador to Portugal, Raimundo Carreiro Silva, wrote in DN that Porto Digital Europa had chosen Aveiro's innovation hub and already had ten companies on board.
ApexBrasil's Lisbon incubator's first class of ten was named at Web Summit 2025, and 20 companies are due to be announced for its 2027 class at the Brazil Pavilion on 10 November.
ApexBrasil gives Brazil's ecosystem as more than 13,000 startups, more than 120 venture capital funds, more than 250 innovation hubs and more than 30 unicorns.
Brasil 61 reported on 31 August 2026 that Brazil had US$2.135 billion of venture capital in 2024 across 386 deals.
